title: Hire velocity risk scenario and async eval kit
body:
Purpose:
This living kit is designed for two simultaneous goals: (1) give people-ops and hiring managers a compact scenario-based forecast for hire velocity risk (i.e., what happens to team capacity if we hit hiring slowdowns, freezes, or sudden ramp needs), and (2) provide an asynchronous interview and scoring template that reduces scheduling friction and improves calibration when bandwidth is constrained.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: hiring managers, recruiters, interviewers, people-ops partners.
- Scope: engineering, product, infra and platform IC hires across early-to-mid levels (L2–L5).
- Use cases: hiring freeze contingency planning, rapid refill after attrition, cross-team interview pooling, and decentralized asynchronous interviewing.

Section A — Hire velocity risk scenarios (quick model):
1) Inputs we use: active reqs, avg time-to-offer (TTO), offer acceptance rate, onboarding time to independent contribution (OTIC), and current backlog velocity (story points/week or PR throughput).
2) Baseline snapshot (example):
   - Active reqs: 14
   - Avg TTO: 34 days
   - Offer accept rate: 78%
   - OTIC: 8 weeks
   - Team backlog velocity: 120 points/week

3) Three scenarios to run quickly (templates below):
   - Slowdown: hiring rate drops by 50% for 8 weeks (simulate hires falling out and extended TTO)
   - Freeze: hiring stops for 12 weeks; prioritize internal reorg and temporary contractors
   - Surge: need to double hires for 6 weeks (e.g., new product launch) — plan for fast interviews and contractor bridge

Quick template to compute impact (spreadsheet-friendly):
   - Column A: scenario name
   - Column B: Expected hires started during period
   - Column C: Expected hires fully onboarded (after OTIC)
   - Column D: Capacity delta (compared to baseline)
   - Column E: Recommended mitigations (temp reassign, contractors, deprioritize roadmap)

Decision triggers (example):
   - If capacity delta < -20% for >4 weeks => escalate to GTM and product leadership
   - If hire velocity remains <70% baseline for >6 weeks => consider targeted offers (signing bonuses) and prioritize critical roles

Section B — Asynchronous interview & eval kit (how we run async without losing fidelity):
Goals: speed up interview loops while retaining signal quality and calibration. Use when scheduling interviews is the primary bottleneck or when cross-timezone collaboration is required.

1) Roles suitable for async: mid-level ICs with well-defined technical exercises, product managers for take-home prompts, and infra roles with ops runbooks. Not recommended for senior ICs (>L5) or org/people-manager hires.

2) Async flow (standardized):
   - Step 0: Hiring manager posts a 48–72 hour take-home task with clear deliverables and a rubric.
   - Step 1: Candidate submits artifact + short self-review (500 words max) + time spent estimate.
   - Step 2: Two interviewers (paired async reviewers) evaluate using the scorecard below. Each reviewer has 72 hours to submit.
   - Step 3: Synthesis: hiring manager reviews scores and readouts, schedules a 30-min sync only if variance > 2 points on any core competency.

3) Async scorecard (numeric, 1–5 where 1=Insufficient, 3=Meets bar, 5=Exceptional). Keep each line item independent and provide 1–2 sentence justification. Required fields in card:
   - Competency: Technical correctness and tradeoffs (scale 1–5)
   - Competency: Design and system thinking (scale 1–5)
   - Competency: Communication and clarity (scale 1–5)
   - Competency: Ownership and initiative (scale 1–5)
   - Competency: Security/privacy/operational considerations (scale 1–5; N/A allowed)
   - Overall recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / Consider with concerns / No hire
   - Time spent evaluating: X hours

Calibration notes: reviewers must add a 1–2 sentence explicit red-flag or green-flag note. Do not use only numeric scores — textual signal is essential.

Section C — Rapid interview rubrics (compact examples, tailored by role):
A. Backend engineer (L3–L4) rubric highlights:
   - Core skills: algorithmic problem solving (breadth, approach), system design for 10k–100k TPS (capability to reason about bottlenecks), debugging/live debugging examples (process over memorized solutions).
   - Behavioral anchors: ownership example in past 12 months, handling ambiguity, trade-off calls.
   - Red flags: refuses to surface assumptions, no postmortem learning, over-focus on micro-optimizations with no product context.

B. Product manager rubric highlights:
   - Strategy signal: clear user problem definition, prioritized metrics, go-to-market considerations.
   - User empathy: evidence of talking to customers and learning.
   - Delivery: example of tradeoffs and shipping under constraints.

C. Infra/platform engineer rubric highlights:
   - Ops mindset: incident runbook contributions, SLO thinking, capacity planning examples.
   - Security & cost: awareness of trade-offs and mitigation steps.

Section D — Offer & compensation quick calibration (when velocity matters):
- Use a small fast-track panel: hiring manager + recruiter + one senior eng (comp calibration) to sign off on exceptions.
- Recommended emergency levers: limited signing bonuses, 90-day performance review clause, contractor to perm bridging contracts.
- Approval thresholds: keep documented in case of audit.

Section E — Minimal day-zero and first-30 checklist (for fast fills):
Day zero (before first day):
  - Account creation requests submitted (email, Slack, workspace permissions)
  - Manager sends welcome note with first-week objectives and key teammates
  - Hardware procurement status (laptop imaged / cloud account access)

First week (goal: unblock contributor):
  - 1:1 with manager scheduled daily for first 3 days
  - Small first task assigned (<=2 days) that touches codebase and CI
  - Buddy assigned for onboarding questions with explicit overlap hours

First 30 days (goal: independent small feature/bug):
  - Shipping checklist: PR merged + QA + short retro with manager
  - Learning checklist: core architecture doc read, infra on-call primer, security checklist complete
  - Feedback checkpoint: 30-day written feedback from manager and buddy

Section F — Risk log & mitigation playbook (short):
   - Risk: Candidate ghosting after offer — Mitigation: hold final interviews earlier in loop, recruiter follow-ups at time boundaries, backup short-list.
   - Risk: Async eval disagreement — Mitigation: tie-break sync with hiring manager, require third reviewer.
   - Risk: Ramp slower than OTIC estimate — Mitigation: temporary scope reduction and weekly tracking with engineering manager

Action items (next steps for people-ops):
  - [ ] Convert this kit into a 1-sheet for hiring managers (due 2025-08-09)
  - [ ] Add async scorecard template to our interview templates folder and start a 4-week pilot with 3 teams (eng-platform, product-core, infra)
  - [ ] Run one scenario simulation for two teams and present capacity deltas at next leadership weekly (due 2025-08-16)

Notes and provenance:
- Built from fragments of previous onboarding playbooks and manager interviews; intentionally lightweight so managers can adopt parts without full process change.
- For audit/history: reference linked artifacts above and Jira JIRA-OPS-321 for pilot tracking.
